title: Quasi-coherence of each truncated higher image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and $a,q\in\mathbf Z$. Then the module sheaf $H^q(Rf_*\tau_{\ge a}E)$ is quasi-coherent, where $Rf_*$ is [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $\tau_{\ge a}$ is the standard lower truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

source.place: Lemma 36.4.1 proof, bounded-below paragraph; ordinary higher-image quasi-coherence is Tag 01XJ, part (1)

proof.text: Canonical lower truncation has quasi-coherent cohomology and vanishes below a, using the standard t-structure and the zero quasi-coherent module.

The bounded-below truncation hypercohomology spectral sequence has E2 terms ordinary higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules, which are quasi-coherent for qcqs morphisms; negative or below-bound terms vanish. Kernel, image and cokernel closure gives quasi-coherence on every page.
The finite convergent filtration of the abutment has stable page terms as quasi-coherent graded pieces; extension closure and descending induction prove quasi-coherence of the abutment.

mathlib_searches.query: The cohomology sheaves of the derived pushforward of a lower truncated quasi coherent complex along a qcqs morphism are quasi coherent
Higher direct images of bounded below complexes with quasi coherent cohomology are quasi coherent under quasi compact quasi separated scheme morphisms
